transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep jumping out of my skin at work. A breaker snaps, a tool hits the floor, or somebody comes up behind me, and my heart just starts pounding. It keeps going long after everybody else has moved on.
Did this jumpiness start after any particular frightening, dangerous, or traumatic event happened to you, either at work or elsewhere?
Yeah. It started after an arc-flash accident on a retrofit job. That was about a year and a month ago.
Since the accident, have you had any unwanted memories, nightmares, or moments where you suddenly feel like you're re-living the arc-flash event, even when you're safe and it's not happening?

Yeah. It can come out of nowhere. I’ll be loading tools in the truck and suddenly see that flash again, or hear the trainee yelling. For a second it hits me like it’s happening all over again, and it knocks me sideways.
Since the accident, have you been avoiding certain places, activities, or conversations that remind you of the arc-flash event?

Yeah. I make excuses not to go near certain panels or breakers, and I try to avoid some job sites if I can. Even talking about that day—I’d rather not, because once it starts in my head, I can’t shut it off.

Since the accident, have you noticed changes in how you feel overall—like feeling numb, distant from people you care about, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or having persistent negative thoughts about yourself or the world?
Yeah. Mostly I’m just mad and guilty all the time. Like I failed that kid, and everybody can see it on me.
